result.summary:
Scope test: Step 2's artifacts_out is real behavioral surface -- two new scheduled jobs (apps/bot/src/scheduler/urgencyJobs.ts, apps/bot/src/scheduler/autoDeclineJobs.ts) that write real registrations/audit_log/notification_ledger rows and send real (fake-captured) messages, plus a new pure predicate (isRequestUrgent) and a new list-read field (PendingRequestListItem.isUrgent). Full Steps 3b/4 apply -- not a docs-only requirement. BACKEND-DEV wrote zero automated tests for this requirement (confirmed: its step-02 handoff's artifacts_out lists no *.test.ts/*.db.test.ts file), so per decisions/0006 and docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-035.md's established precedent, this step writes the full runnable test source for two new files in docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-036.md -- TEST-RUNNER creates the actual files verbatim from that markdown at Step 4, once TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR passes this design.

All 8 acceptance criteria mapped to concrete, runnable cases (AC-to-case table at the top of the spec):
- AC1 (T-48h boundary, both timings): File 1 (urgencyJobs.db.test.ts) describe('AC1') -- an event exactly 48h from starts_at with two 'requested' registrations is pushed to the chapter's organizer AND both items are marked isUrgent=true on listPendingRequestsForOrganizer; a second event 49h out (constructed in the SAME test, so both timings genuinely run) surfaces neither the push nor the marker.
- AC2 (mass transition at close): File 2 (autoDeclineJobs.db.test.ts) describe('AC2') -- 3 pending + 1 approved-in-advance + 1 rejected-in-advance; runs the job once; asserts exactly 3 admission->'rejected' transitions, exactly 3 sends, exactly one ledger row and one audit_log row (actorUserId null) per transitioned registration, and the admitted/already-rejected rows completely untouched (zero new audit_log rows for either).
- AC3 (honest wording): File 2 describe('AC3') -- reads the actual captured message text and asserts it contains the 'was not decided before registration closed' / 'Nobody reviewed and declined it' substrings, asserts it does NOT contain personal-merit phrasings ('you were not accepted', 'not good enough', 'not qualified', 'your application'), and contains the exact reused catalog.event.deepLinkSeeUpcoming onward-path string.
- AC4 (restart-safety, the hardest one): File 2 describe('AC4') -- calls the SAME job instance's .run(evaluationTime) TWICE (not once): run 1 transitions and sends for all 3 pending registrations (asserted individually); run 2, same evaluationTime, asserts sent.length is STILL 3 (zero further sends), all 3 rows are still 'rejected' with zero further audit_log rows, and each registration still has exactly one (not two) ledger row. A dedicated design note in the spec traces why this is the correct restart-safety proof: it mirrors scheduler/noShowJobs.db.test.ts's own already-established REQ-032 AC3 pattern (two .run() calls at the same evaluationTime, no literal process kill needed) and cites docs/agents/design/REQ-036.md §4's own trace that the two guarding mechanisms (admission='requested' re-selection filter; notification_ledger's unique index) hold regardless of whether the second call is caused by a genuine restart or a repeated tick.
- AC5 (registration_closes_at IS NULL): File 2 describe('AC5'), two cases -- an event with registrationClosesAt=null whose endsAt has already passed is auto-declined exactly as a non-null close would be (no crash, no silent skip, registrationClosesAt confirmed still null/no column added); a second case confirms the SAME null-registrationClosesAt event evaluated BEFORE endsAt is NOT yet auto-declined (proves the fallback is time-gated on endsAt, not unconditional).
- AC6 (audit): verified inline in File 2's AC2/AC4/AC5 cases (audit-row count captured before and after via countAuditRows(), actorUserId asserted null on every auto_decline row) -- no separate describe block, since AC6 is a property of the exact same writes those cases already exercise, not a distinct code path; noted explicitly in the AC-to-case map rather than silently omitted.
- AC7 (blocked-skip / broadcast_opt_in-ignored, both sends): File 1 describe('AC7') for the urgency side (chapter X's broadcastOptIn=false organizer is pushed exactly once; chapter Y's blocked=true organizer receives nothing and gets no ledger row) + File 2 describe('AC7') for the auto-decline side (registrant A broadcastOptIn=false receives exactly one message; registrant B blocked=true receives none but the state transition + audit row still happen, since the write is not gated on notification success).
- AC8 (catalog-only, ru/en parity, provisional-wording disclosure): File 2 describe('AC8') greps both new scheduler files' actual source for a getCatalog(lang)/catalog.autoDecline.notification call and asserts neither file hardcodes the provisional English sentences as inline literals. The ru/en key-set parity half is intentionally NOT re-tested here -- apps/bot/src/i18n/catalogs.test.ts's existing 'ru and en have identical key sets' test already re-runs against the full flattened catalog on every npm test and already covers these new keys structurally; adding a duplicate assertion would be exactly the 'check with nothing real to fail against' busywork the role file forbids. The disclosure half (handoff records wording as provisional) was verified directly by reading handoffs/WF02-REQ-036/step-02-backend-dev.json's result.issues[0], which explicitly states the three new strings are 'placeholder copy pending product-owner review' -- confirmed present, not merely assumed from this spec's own restatement, per REQ-014/031/032 precedent for process-shaped ACs.

tg_id ranges claimed, confirmed distinct via grep -rn 'let nextTgId\|let tgSeq' apps/bot/src against every existing band (highest prior: 1_021_000_000, apps/bot/src/handlers/organizerRequests.db.test.ts): apps/bot/src/scheduler/urgencyJobs.db.test.ts uses 1_030_000_000+; apps/bot/src/scheduler/autoDeclineJobs.db.test.ts uses 1_031_000_000+.

ISS-0014 execution note carried into the spec: both new files must run under npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism, no case concurrent with any other DB-backed file against the same scratch Postgres. ISS-0031 note carried into the spec: a full-suite run may need a retry for a conclusive signal per BACKEND-DEV's own step-02 handoff; this changes how TEST-RUNNER interprets a flaky-looking full-suite failure, not what these cases check.
